results.title: Central-range large-prime criterion from the square-root split bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $4 \le r$ and $2r \le N$, and write $r\#$ for the product of the primes at most $r$. If $r \cdot N^{\lfloor \sqrt{N} \rfloor + 1} \cdot r\# < 4^r$, then $\binom{N}{r}$ has a prime divisor $p$ with $p > r$.

results.title: Large-prime criterion from the square-root split bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $0 < N$ and $r \le N$, and write $r\#$ for the product of the primes at most $r$. If $r! \cdot N^{\lfloor \sqrt{N} \rfloor + 1} \cdot r\# < (N + 1 - r)^r$, then $\binom{N}{r}$ has a prime divisor $p$ with $p > r$.

results.title: Large-prime criterion from the prime-counting bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $0 < N$ and $r \le N$, and let $\pi(r)$ be the number of primes at most $r$. If $r! \cdot N^{\pi(r)} < (N + 1 - r)^r$, then $\binom{N}{r}$ has a prime divisor $p$ with $p > r$.

results.title: Large-prime criterion from the half-plus-one exponent bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $0 < N$ and $r \le N$. If $r! \cdot N^{\lfloor r/2 \rfloor + 1} < (N + 1 - r)^r$, then $\binom{N}{r}$ has a prime divisor $p$ with $p > r$.

results.title: Large-prime criterion from the 3r/8 exponent bound

results.title: Power-only large-prime criterion from the 3r/8 exponent bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $0 < N$, $38 \le r$ and $r \le N$. If $r^r \cdot N^{\lfloor 3r/8 \rfloor} < (N + 1 - r)^r$, then $\binom{N}{r}$ has a prime divisor $p$ with $p > r$.

results.title: Large-prime criterion from the r − 1 exponent bound
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Generating function of odd designated-summand partitions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $k \ge 1$ let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ be the Euler product. This is the integer power series $f_4 f_6^2 / (f_1 f_3 f_{12})$ in $q$, where the denominator $f_1 f_3 f_{12}$ is invertible because its constant coefficient is $1$. It is the generating function $\sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{PD}_2(n) q^n$ of the numbers $\mathrm{PD}_2(n)$ of partitions of $n$ with designated summands into odd parts.

results.title: The odd designated-summand partition function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the integer $\mathrm{PD}_2(n)$ is defined as the coefficient of $q^n$ in the integer power series $f_4 f_6^2 / (f_1 f_3 f_{12})$, where $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ is the Euler product (the denominator has constant coefficient $1$, so it is invertible). It counts the partitions of $n$ with designated summands in which all parts are odd.

results.title: Generating function for partitions with designated summands into odd parts

results.title: IP = PSPACE (Shamir)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The class $\mathsf{IP}$ of decision problems that have interactive proofs (a polynomial-time verifier using polynomially many rounds and random coins, with completeness at least $2/3$ and soundness at most $1/3$ against every prover) equals the class $\mathrm{PSPACE}$ of decision problems whose languages are decided by multi-tape Turing machines in polynomial space.

results.title: Allele frequency at the first locus

results.title: Linkage disequilibrium of a two-locus gamete law
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The linkage disequilibrium `D = x_AB x_ab - x_Ab x_aB`.

results.title: Random mating with recombination
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: One generation of random mating with recombination fraction `r`: `recombine r x g = (1 - r) x_g + r p_{g.1} q_{g.2}`.

results.title: Classical form of the recombination recursion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The classical form of the recursion: coupling gametes (`AB`, `ab`) lose `r D` and repulsion gametes (`Ab`, `aB`) gain `r D`. This identity holds for every real `r`; the biological domain is `0 ≤ r ≤ 1/2`.

results.title: Recombination preserves total gamete frequency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Recombination keeps gamete frequencies summing to `1`.

results.title: Recombination preserves nonnegativity of gamete frequencies
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Recombination keeps gamete frequencies nonnegative for `0 ≤ r ≤ 1`.

results.title: Recombination preserves first-locus allele frequencies
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Allele frequencies at the first locus are unchanged by random mating (for every real `r`).

results.title: Recombination preserves second-locus allele frequencies
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Allele frequencies at the second locus are unchanged by random mating (for every real `r`).

results.title: Linkage disequilibrium decays by the factor $1 - r$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Linkage disequilibrium decays by the factor `1 - r` per generation: `D' = (1 - r) D` (for every real `r`).

results.title: Linkage disequilibrium after $t$ generations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: After `t` generations, `D_t = (1 - r)^t D_0`.

results.title: Linkage disequilibrium tends to zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Linkage disequilibrium tends to `0` whenever `0 < r ≤ 1`; this contains the biological range `0 < r ≤ 1/2`. For `r = 0` (complete linkage) `D` is constant.

results.title: Haldane's map function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Haldane's map function `r(d) = (1 - e^{-2d}) / 2`: the recombination fraction between two loci at map distance `d` Morgans when crossovers form a Poisson process (no interference).

results.title: Series for the probability of an odd Poisson count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The probability that a Poisson count of mean `d` is odd, as a series: `∑_{k odd} e^{-d} d^k / k! = (1 - e^{-2d}) / 2` (Haldane 1919). The series identity holds for every real `d`; it is a probability for `0 ≤ d`.

results.title: Haldane's map function from Poisson crossovers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Haldane's map function (Haldane 1919): if the number of crossovers in an interval of map length `d` Morgans is Poisson with mean `d`, the probability of an odd number of crossovers, i.e. of recombination between the ends of the interval, is `(1 - e^{-2d}) / 2`.

results.title: Nonnegativity of Haldane's map function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Haldane's map function is nonnegative at nonnegative distances.

results.title: Haldane's recombination fraction is below one half
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The recombination fraction is always below `1/2` (for every real `d`).

results.title: Distant loci are unlinked in the limit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Loci far apart are unlinked in the limit: `r → 1/2` as `d → ∞`.

results.title: Inverse Haldane map function recovers map distance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The inverse map function `d = -½ log(1 - 2r)` recovers the map distance.

results.title: Every recombination fraction below one half is attained
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every `r < 1/2` is the recombination fraction at the distance `-½ log(1 - 2r)`. The hypothesis keeps `log` on positive arguments: at `r = 1/2` the right side would use the junk value `log 0 = 0`. The distance is nonnegative exactly when `0 ≤ r`.

results.title: Phenotypic covariance of a linear mixed model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The phenotypic covariance `V = Z G Zᵀ + R` of the linear mixed model `y = X b + Z u + e` with `Cov u = G`, `Cov e = R`.

results.title: Solution of Henderson's mixed-model equations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Henderson's mixed-model equations for `y = X b + Z u + e`, `Cov u = G`, `Cov e = R`: `[Xᵀ R⁻¹ X, Xᵀ R⁻¹ Z; Zᵀ R⁻¹ X, Zᵀ R⁻¹ Z + G⁻¹] [b; u] = [Xᵀ R⁻¹ y; Zᵀ R⁻¹ y]`.

results.title: Positive definiteness of the phenotypic covariance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `V = Z G Zᵀ + R` is positive definite.

results.title: Henderson's mixed-model equations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Henderson's mixed-model equations (Henderson 1975; Robinson 1991): for positive definite `G` and `R` and `V = Z G Zᵀ + R`, `(b, u)` solves the mixed-model equations if and only if `b` solves the generalized least-squares normal equations `Xᵀ V⁻¹ X b = Xᵀ V⁻¹ y` and `u = G Zᵀ V⁻¹ (y - X b)`.

results.title: The MME solution is the GLS estimate and the BLUP
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The MME solution is the GLS estimate and the BLUP (Henderson 1975): if moreover `Xᵀ V⁻¹ X` is invertible, the mixed-model equations have the unique solution `b̂ = (Xᵀ V⁻¹ X)⁻¹ Xᵀ V⁻¹ y` (the GLS estimate) and `û = G Zᵀ V⁻¹ (y - X b̂)`.

results.title: BLUP as a conditional law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: BLUP as a conditional law (Henderson 1975; Robinson 1991): in the Gaussian mixed model `y = X b + Z u + e` with fixed effects `b`, random effects `u ~ N(0, G)` and residuals `e ~ N(0, R)` independent, `G` and `R` positive definite, the conditional law of `u` given `y` is `N(G Zᵀ V⁻¹ (y - X b), G - G Zᵀ V⁻¹ Z G)` with `V = Z G Zᵀ + R` (for almost every `y`).

results.title: BLUP is the conditional expectation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: BLUP is the conditional expectation in the Gaussian mixed model: `𝔼[u | y] = G Zᵀ V⁻¹ (y - X b)` almost surely.

results.title: The LDpred-inf posterior
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The LDpred-inf posterior (Vilhjálmsson et al. 2015; the likelihood `β̂ | β ~ N(R β, R / N)` of Zhu and Stephens 2017): with `M` markers, `N` individuals, heritability `h² > 0`, effects `β ~ N(0, h² / M · I)`, an LD matrix `R` that is positive definite, and marginal estimates `β̂ = R β + ε` with `ε ~ N(0, R / N)` independent of `β`, the posterior law of `β` given `β̂` is…

results.title: Marginal association estimate of a marker
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The `N`-normalized marginal association estimate `β̂_j = X_jᵀ y / N` of marker `j` for the phenotype `y = X β + ε` (fixed effects `β`, noise `ε`).

results.title: The mean of the marginal estimates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The mean of the marginal estimates (Zhu and Stephens 2017): for fixed effects `β` and noise with mean zero, `𝔼[X_jᵀ y / N] = (R β)_j` with `R = Xᵀ X / N` (`ldCorr`).

results.title: The raw residual-product second moment of the marginal estimates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The raw residual-product second moment of the marginal estimates (Zhu and Stephens 2017): if `𝔼[ε_i ε_i'] = σ² [i = i']`, then `𝔼[(β̂_j - (R β)_j)(β̂_k - (R β)_k)] = σ² / N · R_jk`.
